chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim from 'Ali from Abu Basir said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married off his slave woman to a free man or to the slaves of another group. He said: 'He does not have the right to take her back (from her husband). If he sells her, and the one who bought her wishes to take her back from her husband, then he may do so.' He said: 'He did so.'
ai.seo_question: Can a master divorce his slave woman from her free husband, and what happens if he sells her?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the stability of marriage contracts for slave women (*Ummahat al-Awlad* or *Mukataba* contexts), establishing that a master cannot unilaterally dissolve the union by merely changing her status. It introduces a specific legal nuance: while the master retains the marriage, the act of sale transfers the right of *Khiyar al-Taba'ah* (option of separation) to the new owner, who may choose to keep the couple together or separate them, reflecting the interplay between ownership rights and marital sanctity in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the principle that marriage is a binding contract that persists unless actively dissolved by the holder of the right of separation.
